To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose DelugeNets, a class of neural networks with massive and flexible cross-layer information inflow, and demonstrate their superior performances on CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet datasets; 2) the proposed DelugeNets outperform existing ResNet models in both classification accuracy and parameter efficiency.

we propose a novel deep neural network architecture, named DelugeNet, which can achieve state-of-the-art classification accuracies on CIFAR- 10/100 and comparable accuracies on ImageNet with fewer parameters, and that DelugeNet can also achieve better accuracies on CIFARI0/100 with the same number of parameters as ResNet-200.

we propose DelugeNets, a class of neural networks with flexible cross-layer connections and massive information inflows from previous layers to succeeding layers, which can achieve superior performance with fewer parameters than existing ResNet models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to efficiently establish connections between different layers in deep neural networks and how to facilitate massive cross-layer information flows.
how to design neural networks that can effectively utilize massive cross-layer information flows.
how to design a deep network with massive and flexible information inflows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DelugeNets provide an effective and efficient way of utilizing the massive cross-layer connectivity to achieve superior performance on various tasks.
the DelugeNets, with their unique cross-layer connections and massive information inflows, can effectively utilize network parameters to achieve better performance.
DelugeNets provide a novel and efficient way to build large-scale networks, and are a promising alternative to ResNets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DelugeNets provide a novel way to build deeper neural networks, which can achieve better performance with less parameters, and thus are more efficient.
DelugeNets, by virtue of massive cross-layer information flows, can achieve state-of-the-art accuracies with fewer parameters and computations.
DelugeNets provide a new perspective on the design of deep learning models, which is more flexible in information inflows, and more effective in parameter utilization.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, the massive and flexible information inflows across layers are beneficial for the performance of deep networks, and the cross-layer convolutional layers with adaptive filters can be used as an efficient mechanism for establishing these connections.
, by allowing massive cross-layer information flows, DelugeNests are more effective at utilizing network parameters, and thus are more parameter efficient than the existing ResNet models.

, the massive cross-layer inflows of information can be beneficial to neural networks, and DelugeNets serve as a promising direction towards the development of neural networks with more efficient and flexible information propagation mechanisms.
